newsitem.title: USA: Unocal to sell venture stake for $250 million.
newsitem.headline: Unocal to sell venture stake for $250 million.

text.p: Unocal Corp. said Thursday it would sell half of an oil refining and marketing venture in the Midwest to co-owner Petroleos de Venezuela, the Venezuelan state-owned oil company, for $250 million.

The venture, Uno-Ven Co., markets "76" brand products throughout the Midwest. The planned sale was the latest step by Unocal to transform itself from an integrated oil company to one involved mainly in oil and gas exploration and production.
Earlier this month, El Segundo, Calif.-based Unocal agreed to sell its West Coast refining, marketing and transportation assets to Tosco Corp. for about $2 billion.

"This transaction would complete Unocal's transition from a vertically integrated oil company to being the world's largest independent oil and gas producer and an important developer of energy projects overseas," Unocal Chairman Roger Beach said.
The 50-50 partnership between Unocal and Petroleos de Venezuela was formed in 1989.

Under the deal, Unocal said all of Uno-Ven's oil refining and marketing assets will be sold to units of the Venezuelan company. Unocal owns the 50 percent Uno-Ven stake through its Midwest 76 Inc. subsidiary.

Uno-Ven owns and operates a 153,000-barrel-a-day refinery near Chicago and supplies about 2,500 independently owned "76" retail outlets in 15 states, mostly in the Midwest. The partnership has 1,100 employees and annual sales of more than $1.2 billion.
The venture also owns a lubricants blending and packaging plant in Cincinnati and two lubricant distribution terminals.
Uno-Ven buys the crude oil for its refinery under a long-term contract with an affiliate of the Venezuelan company.
Unocal said it expected to invest a portion of the proceeds from the sale in exploration and development projects overseas and in strengthening its oil and gas operations in the Gulf of Mexico.
Affiliates of the Venezuelan company will assume all liability for Uno-Ven debt, Unocal said.
